test_name: Validate Error Message for Invalid Login
description: This scenario tests the error handling of the login form when an invalid email or password is used. It ensures proper error messages are displayed without creating a session.
steps: 2. Verify the visibility of the email and password input fields.
3. Verify the visibility of the 'Log In' button and ensure it is enabled.
4. Enter an invalid email into the email input field.
5. Enter a valid password into the password input field.
7. Verify that an error message is displayed saying 'Invalid email or password.'
8. Clear the email and password fields.
9. Enter a valid email into the email input field.
10. Enter an invalid password into the password input field.
12. Verify that the same error message is displayed.
13. Clear both input fields and leave them empty.
15. Verify that the error message indicates that both fields are required.
expected_results: An error message 'Invalid email or password.' is displayed when invalid credentials are used.
No session token is created if login fails.
The error message is cleared when the input fields are updated.
edge_cases: Submit the form with only one field filled.
Submit the form with both fields empty.
Submit the form with special characters in the email field.
Submit the form with a valid email but incorrect password multiple times consecutively.
Submit the form with a SQL injection attempt in the email field.
dependencies: The invalid email must not exist in the system.
The server must handle incorrect login attempts correctly.
The error message element must be visible and accessible.
performance_metrics: Time taken for the error message to appear after submission.
CPU usage when validating input on the client-side.
accessibility_requirements: Ensure error messages are properly announced by screen readers.
Verify the form fields have associated hint text for invalid state.
